symptom: Re-running `create or modify microflow|nanoflow` with only a filter's expression changed gave the activity, its ListOperationsAction and its FilterByExpression new $IDs, while a decision whose condition changed the same way kept its own; exec printed `spliced: 1 replaced` for both, and check, mx check, diff and describe were clean, so only a BSON dump or Studio Pro's version control (one activity removed, another added) showed it
cause: The statement diff turns a changed activity into a Replace, and Mutator.Replace at top level appended the fragment's freshly built activity and removed the stored one. The in-place swaps that existed (swapInPlace: loop bodies #1106, handled activities #1489) kept the stored slot and geometry but still wrote the fragment's $IDs. The patch write (UpdateRawUnitPatch) deliberately skips canon.TransplantIDs, so nothing downstream re-paired them. Separately, two adjacent changed activities form one run, which became 'replace the first by both, drop the second' and could never be an edit
file: mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice_edit.go (sameKind, swapKeeping, editInPlace, carryPairs, pairEntries, applyCarried), mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice.go (Replace, replaceInLoop, replaceKeepingHandler, Bytes), mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (noteEdited), mdl/executor/cmd_flow_modify.go (patchSummary, pairwiseSameKind)
fix: A replace by one activity of the same activity and action $Type is written into the stored slot and paired structurally with the stored activity: same $Type at the same key, list entries by what they name (Attribute/Association plus Type, Parameter, LanguageCode, Name, Key), unnamed entries by position only for equal $Type sequences. The pairs are applied at Bytes over every binary in the unit, so the executor can keep naming the fragment's $ID (LinkNote of a stored note) until then. MicroflowMutator.EditedInPlace feeds the report: `edited in place` vs `replaced with new element IDs`. A run of N changed statements pairwise of one plain kind is split into N one-for-one gaps
test: mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice_edit_in_place_test.go (six kinds byte-exact, members by name, another kind/operation is new, notes, loop body, error handler); mdl/executor/flow_splice_edit_in_place_1761_pedapp_test.go (six kinds x microflow/nanoflow on the real codec, a control that a log for a filter is new, and PedApp's Studio Pro-authored PopulateUserAttributes edited in one run). With the carry stubbed out the engine and executor tests fail with new $IDs; measured on 10.24.24: unfixed 1ccaa1aa->1c24b792 for the activity, fixed all kept, mx check 0 errors
insight: The identity carry has to happen where the pairing is known, and that is the splice, not canon: the patch writer is told the splice owns its $IDs (ContentsOwnElementIDs), so a fix that hopes Reconcile will re-pair finds it switched off on purpose. Pair by name before position — a member list paired by index hands a removed member's $ID to its neighbour, which is the GUID-class mistake one level down. And apply the carry late: the executor still names the fragment's $IDs after Replace returns (linkStoredNotes draws a stored note's line to the fragment's activity), so the stored $IDs go on at Bytes, where one pass rewrites every reference too. The report half matters as much: a count that prints 'replaced' for both outcomes is why the bug read as harmless; the test that a decision 'kept its IDs' and a filter did not was only visible in a BSON dump
